title: Why every team should go async
description: Why every team should go async
transcript: I personally, once again, still believe that a lot of meetings are unnecessary. So if you could get the same amount of whatever you're looking for out of that meeting from asynchronous communication, I would always do that. So, for example, if you're doing a meeting just to, like, get an update on where the clients are at, whatever else it is, you could instead create a good client success system and maybe a good score card where you could just see, okay, only report on the clients that are at. Let's just say you have a score card of 1 to 10 that are a below a 6. I need you to report on all those clients. So majority of your clients are probably doing great, but then maybe 10% are having problems. And so then even if you kept the meeting, you could be only talking about two clients versus like 20 clients, which is what we used to do. We should go through every single client one by one, and then it's like, okay, if less than 10% of clients are having problems, then we probably should just talk about the problem clients. I think there's a huge benefit of, like, asynchronous communication today's day and age, which is essentially communication where people don't have to be together on a meeting.
